name: Acquired Angioedema with C1 Inhibitor Deficiency

criteria.description: Reduced functional and antigenic C1 inhibitor levels in plasma
No family history of hereditary angioedema
Identification of underlying lymphoproliferative or autoimmune disorder
Recurrent episodes of non-pruritic, non-pitting angioedema without urticaria

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent angioedema attacks without urticaria, low C1 inhibitor levels, low C4 levels, and absence of family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires exclusion of hereditary angioedema and identification of associated disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Facial and peripheral soft tissue swelling
searchTerms: face and limb soft tissue swelling
swelling of face and arms or legs
voice box swelling causing breathing trouble

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain due to gastrointestinal mucosal edema
searchTerms: belly pain from gut lining swelling
abdominal discomfort due to intestinal swelling
stomach pain caused by bowel swelling

common.symptomName: Dyspnea secondary to upper airway edema
searchTerms: shortness of breath from airway swelling
breathing difficulty due to upper airway swelling

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting associated with gastrointestinal edema
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting with gut swelling
throwing up linked to bowel swelling

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy in association with underlying lymphoproliferative disease
searchTerms: nerve damage linked to blood cancer
tingling and numbness with lymph disease
peripheral nerve problems from lymphoproliferative disorder
low blood pressure during severe swelling
blood pressure drop during swelling episodes

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to associated disorders
searchTerms: kidney problems due to related diseases
impaired kidney function secondary to other disorders

laboratory: Low functional and antigenic C1 inhibitor levels
Normal or low C1q levels (distinguishing from hereditary angioedema)
imaging: CT or ultrasound may show bowel wall edema during abdominal attacks
Laryngeal edema visible on neck imaging during acute episodes
genetic: No pathogenic mutations in SERPING1 gene (distinguishes from hereditary angioedema)
other: Detection of underlying lymphoproliferative or autoimmune disorders (e.g., monoclonal gammopathy)
Response to C1 inhibitor concentrate or bradykinin pathway inhibitors

redFlags: Rapid onset laryngeal edema with airway compromise
Recurrent unexplained abdominal pain with vomiting
Absence of urticaria despite severe angioedema
